sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Onslow County?
sections.html:
The Onslow County Tax Office lists, values, bills and collects property tax for the county and for five municipalities. Its Collections Division handles taxes levied by Onslow County, Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro, and it collects vehicle tax for the part of Surf City that lies inside the county.

The office is at 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville and keeps hours Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Phone lines on the county's published list are Administration 910-989-2200, Listings 910-989-2201, Collections 910-989-2202, Land Records 910-989-2204 and Appraisal 910-455-7431. Payment is by cash or check in person, or by card or e-check through the online tax search and payment site, which adds a convenience fee.

A seller should call Collections for a payoff figure, because a town bill and a county bill may be separate lines on one parcel. Land Records answers questions about parcel boundaries and ownership names.

sections.h2: What is Onslow County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Onslow County is a coastal county of 762.08 square miles of land with 217,175 residents on the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate. That is up 6.2 percent from the April 2020 estimates base and well above the 177,772 counted in 2010. Population density was 268.4 people per square mile in 2020, which is far higher than most counties in the eastern part of the state.

The housing numbers explain why turnover is steady. The county has 91,470 housing units and 75,265 households for 2020 to 2024. The owner occupied rate is 63.7 percent, the median value of owner occupied homes is $236,400, and median gross rent is $1,265. A little over one in five residents moved in the prior year, since 78.7 percent lived in the same house a year earlier. The county has 25,185 veterans and issued 1,372 building permits in 2025. The median household income is $68,148, and 12.8 percent of residents are 65 or older. All figures are from Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: When are Onslow County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1 each year and become delinquent if unpaid after January 5 of the next year. The county's Taxes Due page says real estate and personal property bills are mailed in July, and registered motor vehicle tax is combined with the state's vehicle tax and tag system.

State law backs that calendar. Under G.S. 105-360, a bill paid before January 6 carries no interest, then 2 percent applies through the end of January and three-fourths of one percent a month or part of a month after that. In February the tax collector reports unpaid real property tax to the governing body, and the liens can be advertised between March 1 and June 30 under G.S. 105-369.

The 2026 bills ran later than usual. A county notice dated August 18, 2026 says personal property bills were due to be mailed by the last week of August and real estate notices might not go out until early September, yet the due date stayed September 1, 2026 and delinquency still starts after January 5, 2027.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 revaluation change in Onslow County?
sections.html:
The countywide reappraisal that was set for January 1, 2026 was pushed back one year, so 2026 bills use values from the previous reappraisal. The county's revaluation page explains that two new state laws, Session Law 2026-8 and Session Law 2026-47, require the delay, and the new values take effect in 2027.

Onslow County reappraises on a four year cycle by resolution, which the page says was adopted in 2001 for a revaluation effective January 1, 2006 and every four years after. North Carolina law only requires a reappraisal every eight years, and counties may choose a shorter cycle by resolution.

  • Your 2026 value should generally match 2025, adjusted for new construction or other changes as of January 1, 2026.
  • Your bill can still rise, since the tax rate set by the Board of Commissioners and by any city or fire district also drives it.
  • An appeal already filed against the 2026 reappraisal value stays alive, and the outcome applies when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • The county set December 31, 2026 as the last day to appeal either the value used for this year, the 2026 reappraisal value, or both.

For the 2027 tax year, the usual appeal deadlines and steps return. For the current rate on your parcel, ask the Tax Office or read the rate in the county's adopted budget, since a rate is only final once the Board of Commissioners adopts it.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Onslow County value?
sections.html:
Start by asking the Tax Office for an informal review, then use the formal process under the state Machinery Act if you still disagree. The county's Appeals page says the formal process varies by property type: real estate, personal property or motor vehicles.

Timing differs by type. A property review for a real estate parcel has to be requested before the formal appeals begin in the spring of each year. Personal property reviews must start within 30 days of the bill date for property billed annually, and vehicles must be appealed within 30 days of the bill date.

Appeal steps and deadlines for Onslow County property tax
StageWhat the sources say
Informal reviewContact the Tax Office before formal appeals open in spring (real estate); within 30 days of the bill date (personal property, vehicles)
County boardThe county commissioners usually sit as the board of equalization and review, first meeting not earlier than the first Monday in April and not later than the first Monday in May
Hearing requestIn writing or in person before the board adjourns, or within 15 days after the decision notice was mailed if that notice came fewer than 15 days before adjournment
State levelNotice of appeal to the Property Tax Commission within 30 days after the board mailed its decision

The table draws on the county Appeals page and G.S. 105-322 and 105-290. Because the 2026 schedule was altered by the new laws, confirm dates with the Tax Office before relying on the usual spring calendar.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs apply?
sections.html:
The county page on exemptions points to deferment and exclusion options and a military exemption page. State law sets the main programs, and an owner may receive the benefit of only one of the three programs below.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50 percent of appraised value of a permanent residence, for an owner who is at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled and within the income limit. The 2026 income limit is $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income limit.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4 percent of income up to the income limit, or 5 percent of income above it up to $58,200 for 2026, with the excess deferred as a lien.

File Form AV-9 with the county assessor. It should be filed during the January listing period and must be accepted through June 1 before the tax year. The circuit breaker needs a new application each year. Deferred taxes for the preceding three fiscal years come due if the owner sells, so a seller using that program should ask the Tax Office for the full payoff before listing.

For active duty military, the county's Military Exemptions page covers personal property such as vehicles, boats and mobile homes. It asks service members who claim another home of record to supply a current Leave and Earnings Statement each year at tag renewal.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell with property tax unpaid?
sections.html:
The tax is a lien on the parcel from the listing date, and it must be paid or paid off for the buyer to take clear title. Interest and costs attach at the same time. If a bill stays unpaid, the lien can be advertised and foreclosed under G.S. 105-374 or 105-375, with a county Collections office answering which route it uses.

A sale before that point lets you pick the price and timing. Ask Collections for a payoff figure that lists each taxing unit and an end date, because interest changes as of January 6 and again after February 1. The deed itself carries an excise tax of one dollar per $500 of value, paid by the seller to the register of deeds, plus the recording fees in G.S. 161-10. If the house is vacant, inherited or in need of repairs, a cash buyer such as Cash Home Buyers can make an as-is offer that you can set against the payoff and these costs.

faqs.q: When are Onslow County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1 each year. They become delinquent if unpaid on or after January 6, meaning not paid on or before January 5 of the next year, and interest runs from there under G.S. 105-360.

faqs.q: Where is the Onslow County Tax Office?
faqs.a: It is at 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville, open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Call 910-989-2202 for Collections or 910-989-2200 for Administration.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Onslow County property value?
faqs.a: The county's revaluation page says appeals could be filed through December 31, 2026, covering the value used for 2026, the delayed 2026 reappraisal value, or both. For 2027 the normal deadlines apply, so call the Tax Office.

faqs.q: Which towns does the Onslow County Tax Office bill for?
faqs.a: It collects for the county and for Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. For the part of Surf City inside Onslow County it collects vehicle tax only.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax on a house I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes, up to the closing, and any unpaid balance is a lien that the buyer's title search will find. Ask Collections for a payoff and have the closing agent pay it from the proceeds.
